messages:
maria: heads up — eu-west canary alert: a bunch of infra-service pods got evicted during the drain/upgrade step, looks like PDB blocked graceful termination  

devops-bot: deploy status: canary FAILED for infra-service chart=infra-service v2.3.0 namespace=infra canary=eu-west-1  
  checks: pod-health(2/5), pdb-violation(1), image-pull(0)  
  runbook: https://go/release/runbooks/pdb-evictions :robot_face:

ash: can you paste the pdb? my first guess is the chart bumped the PDB to minAvailable: 3 and our canary pool is 2  

maria: yup: ```
NAME               MIN AVAILABLE   MAX UNAVAILABLE   ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS   AGE
infra-service-pdb  3               N/A               0                     12m
```

leo: that explains it — during node drain k8s won't evict if allowed disruptions < 1. Canary only has 2 replicas in eu-west staging pool, so PDB=3 blocks voluntary eviction. Chart change probably tightened PDB in v2.3.0  

ash: options: 1) rollback canary to v2.2.7 (previous chart) 2) patch values for canary release to lower minAvailable / disable pdb 3) manually cordon+force-delete pods (risky)  

ryan-pm: operational constraint: we are in a change window til 17:00 UTC, customer-facing, prefer graceful. What's the shortest safe option?  

sre-oncall: safest is rollback to v2.2.7 and then run a follow-up fix for the chart to make PDB conservative by default. Patching values is fine for a quick canary fix but we risk divergence from default release config.  

leo: I can do a targeted values override for the canary: set `podDisruptionBudget.enabled=false` for the canary release. Patch snippet: ```yaml
pdb:
  enabled: false
```
This keeps the new chart but avoids the blocker while we validate other changes.  

maria: concern: our canary test exercises live rolling drains — if we disable pdb we might hide a regression where pod churn causes service instability. but given the current drain failure blocks the whole canary, disabling temporarily seems reasonable with monitoring guards  

ash: propose plan: 1) apply values override to canary in eu-west: `helm upgrade infra-service ./chart -f canary-eu-west-pdb-override.yaml --namespace infra --set image.tag=2.3.0` 2) re-run deploy-bot canary health check 3) if pass, let canary finish and schedule chart fix PR  

ryan-pm: add to release notes: mention PDB stricter default in 2.3.0 and that we applied a temporary canary override; doc the rollback path if we need to revert  

sre-oncall: I'm on watch. If health-check fails after override we rollback to 2.2.7 immediately: `helm rollback infra-service 3 --namespace infra` (confirm release index before running)  

maria: proceeding with canary override now, will post the `helm` command output  

devops-bot: deploy request received: upgrade infra-service v2.3.0 canary eu-west with values override (pdb.disabled=true). Job id=deploy-7731  

maria: deploy started. re-running smoke tests.  

leo: :eyes: monitoring logs for pod restarts and 5xxs  

maria: smoke tests green, canary progressed to 60% traffic, no p50/p95 regressions observed in the last 10m  

ryan-pm: update release notes draft: "v2.3.0: tightened podDisruptionBudget defaults; temporary canary override applied during rollout — see follow-up PR #452 for permanent config change"  

sre-oncall: marking incident ticket INFRA-2123 and assigning to @ash for chart fix PR, leaving canary to finish. will close ticket after prod rollout and PR merged. :white_check_mark:
